key_insight: Neural networks can efficiently solve the inverse design problem for cascaded-mode near-field landscapes by mapping target optical field patterns to modal coefficients.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable route to design structured near-fields for microscopy and nanoparticle manipulation without relying on manual trial-and-error or direct analytical inversion.
method: Train multilayer neural networks on the relationship between design parameters and near-field landscapes.
Use the trained model for gradient-based optimization to recover modal coefficients that match a target field profile.
Improve harder lateral-field reconstructions with careful training data selection and augmentation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful reconstruction of both simple and complex longitudinal landscapes, with lateral-field results improving after data selection and augmentation.
watch_item: Lateral field inverse design remains more challenging, so performance may depend strongly on the quality and coverage of the training set.
paper_title: Neural Networks for Inverse Design of Cascaded-Mode Near-Field Landscapes
